doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

chapter: Jazz parties, Metropole and San Diego
title: The Metropole in New York
summary: During shipyard bids he spent evenings at the Metropole hearing Hampton, Ellington, Basie, Hawkins, Eldridge and Red Allen.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You got to travel to New York a number of times over the years.
Well I’m a veteran of the Metropole. In 1958, 7 or 8, is when we started pushing the shipyard. And I bid on some ocean going freighters and passenger ships for three lines in

New York, U.S. Lines, Moore McCormick and American Export. And I had to work the Maritime Commission in Washington as well. So I was on a schedule to take me to the east coast two and three times a week. When I was in New York what was involved was going down in the morning, down to where all the marine activity is, calling on somebody, having a drunken lunch with them, and then going back to the hotel to take a nap, and then spend the evening at the place, at the Metropole there. I’ll never forget, there was a bartender there named Blackie who was my buddy. And my secretary back in San Diego knew that if she wanted me, that’s where I’d be. And everybody was there, in those days that’s the only place — you know Ryan’s and all those places were gone. This was the only place that jazz really existed. And hell they’d have the Hampton band and the Ellington band and the Basie band, and oh they got Red Allen, Higginbotham, oh they were all there — Coleman Hawkins, Coleman Hawkins and Roy Eldridge had a group there and they played every night. And there was a big band — you ever been there, the Metropole?

Well there’s a big bandstand behind the bar. And standing room, and then booths along the side. And they’d just change every half hour. And everybody’s having a good time. Red Allen was there greeting everybody at the door when they came in, and it was a wonderful time. Really, if you didn’t like the music you had to like it there. I never realized until later how great it was. I never realized. I thought all these names, you know, and some I didn’t really know well, and later as I collected records I said Jesus, I know this guy. And they just put on a terrific show. Buster Bailey. Remember Buster Bailey?
And he was a friend, Dizzy was there.
